newsitem.title: GERMANY: German policeman kills ex-lover in court shooting.
newsitem.headline: German policeman kills ex-lover in court shooting.

text.p: A German policeman shot dead his estranged common law wife and seriously injured her lawyer in a Frankfurt court on Friday in what was probably a dispute over alimony payments, police said.
The man, 39, pulled out an automatic handgun and fired eight shots at the 33-year-old woman and her female lawyer before giving himself up to police at the scene.
His ex-partner died shortly afterwards in the court and the lawyer was taken to hospital with life-threatening injuries. Neither the man nor the two victims were named.
A woman who saw him being led out of the courthouse in handcuffs said: "He looked really calm. He looked as if he had achieved what he had wanted to achieve, as if he'd been liberated."
Police said they did not yet know the policeman's rank or whether he used his service weapon.
The woman had been suing him for alimony payments after they split up, they said.
It was not clear whether her claim was based on having lived together for a long time or whether they had a child.

"The court hearing was just over in the office of the judge and the parties were still discussing the case with their lawyers when the attacker suddenly pulled out a gun and opened fire," Frankfurt prosecutor Job Tilmann told a news conference.
Tilmann said the man had kept firing until the magazine of his gun was empty. He then gave himself up and was taken away for questioning.

A painter who had been working in the next room told reporters he rushed out when he heard shots being fired in rapid succession. He said there was no panic or screaming but that he had heard what sounded like a brief scuffle.
"I heard shots as if someone was emptying an automatic gun. The guy looked normal when they led him out, just like anyone."
The shooting took place in a court building in Frankfurt's legal district.
